copiapo-san-jose-mine-rescue-2010.summary: On 5 August 2010 a collapse sealed 33 miners 700 metres down in San José copper and gold mine in Chile's Atacama region. They rationed two days of food over 17 days until a percussion drill broke into their refuge on 22 August and brought up a note, 'Estamos bien en el refugio los 33'. Codelco engineers under minister Laurence Golborne ran three parallel drilling plans; Plan B, a Schramm T130 rig with Center Rock downhole hammers operated by Chilean and American crews, reached them on 9 October. On 13 October Fénix 2, a capsule, built by Chilean navy shipyard ASMAR with NASA advice, lifted all 33 in under 24 hours before an estimated billion television viewers. Studies by Useem and Edmondson treat this operation as a case in crisis leadership.

haiti-cholera-un-peacekeepers-2010.summary: In mid-October 2010, nine months after Haiti's earthquake, cholera cases appeared along Artibonite river downstream of a MINUSTAH camp at Mirebalais housing Nepalese troops, in a country with no recorded cholera for a century. Epidemiologist Renaud Piarroux's team mapped early cases to the camp's sewage, and whole-genome sequencing showed Haitian isolates nearly identical to 2010 Nepalese Vibrio cholerae. By 2016 more than 788,000 people had fallen ill and over 9,000 had died; United Nations, which had resisted the link, acknowledged a role in December 2016 under Ban Ki-moon and apologised. Vaccination, water and sanitation drives ended transmission in 2019, but cholera returned in 2022. The outbreak reshaped peacekeeper health screening and debates on UN legal immunity.

hayabusa-sample-return-2010.summary: Launched on an M-V rocket from Uchinoura on 9 May 2003, Hayabusa reaches 535 metre asteroid Itokawa in September 2005, touches down twice in November and loses fuel, attitude control and contact for weeks. On 13 June 2010 its capsule parachutes into Woomera Prohibited Area while main craft burns up. About 1,500 grains under 10 micrometres prove to be Itokawa material, and Tomoki Nakamura's team shows it matches LL ordinary chondrite meteorites, tying a meteorite class to a specific S-type asteroid.

menafrivac-2010.summary: Epidemics of group A meningococcal meningitis swept the Sahel belt from Senegal to Ethiopia every few years; the 2009 season caused about 88,000 cases and 5,000 deaths. After African health ministers rejected a vaccine priced for rich markets, a Meningitis Vaccine Project set up by PATH and WHO in 2001 with 70 million dollars in Gates Foundation money contracted the Serum Institute of India to make a conjugate vaccine for under 50 US cents a dose. Trials from 2005 in The Gambia, Ghana, India, Mali and Senegal showed stronger antibody responses than older polysaccharide vaccines. Burkina Faso began vaccinating first, in December 2010, reaching 12 million people aged 1 to 29 in weeks. Group A cases fell by more than 99 percent in vaccinated areas, and no group A epidemic has occurred there since.

nam-theun-2-dam-laos-2010.summary: Nam Theun 2 Power Company, owned by EDF, Electricity Generating of Thailand and Lao government, brings a 1,070 MW plant into commercial operation in April 2010 after 54 months of construction. Field reports from Mozambique by a Swiss water agency in 2008 and a UNICEF evaluation found children tired, women turning heavy wheels for hours, pumps idle for months awaiting repair and communities asking for their hand pumps back. Sponsors suspended funding in 2009, and in 2010 PlayPumps' sponsor handed remaining stock to Water For People. The case became a standard caution on untested aid technology.

psa-kiwifruit-canker-new-zealand-2010.summary: Pseudomonas syringae pv. actinidiae was confirmed in Bay of Plenty on 5 November 2010. Vanneste's 2017 Annual Review of Phytopathology account estimates costs near 900 million New Zealand dollars and traces likely origin to imported pollen or plant material; his 2010 and 2012 papers characterised strains. Growers cut out Hort16A and grafted Gold3 (SunGold), bred by Plant and Food Research, which proved tolerant; industry exceeded pre-Psa earnings by 2016. Growers' negligence suit against Ministry for Primary Industries succeeded at first instance in 2018 but was overturned on appeal.

In 2011 Glorot's group described advantages over sigmoid and tanh, and found that deep networks trained with ReLU could perform strongly without unsupervised pre-training, especially on large supervised tasks. It avoids vanishing gradients and is now one of the most used activation functions.

It targeted Siemens industrial control systems at Iran's uranium-enrichment plant at Natanz, making centrifuges spin themselves apart while reporting normal readings. The New York Times reported in 2012 that it was a joint US and Israeli operation.

Those uprisings began in Tunisia in late 2010, after Mohamed Bouazizi set himself on fire, and spread in 2011. Facebook and Twitter helped Egyptian and Tunisian activists coordinate protests and circulate information, though social-media use rose after protests began; nine in ten Egyptians and Tunisians polled said they used Facebook to organize protests or spread awareness. Social media contributed to those uprisings but did not cause them alone.

bkash-mobile-money-2011.summary: bKash, a subsidiary of BRAC Bank founded by Kamal and Iqbal Quadir with Money in Motion, launched in July 2011 under Bangladesh Bank's 2011 mobile financial services guidelines. Customers open wallets with basic phones using USSD menus and cash in or out at small shop agents. By 2014 it had 15 million accounts and over 100,000 agents, carrying garment wages, remittances from city to village and bill payments where bank branches were scarce. International Finance Corporation, Gates Foundation and Ant Group later took stakes. bKash became Bangladesh's dominant payments brand and a model for bank-led mobile money, in contrast to telecom-led M-Pesa in Kenya.

Their strain carries a tetracycline-repressible lethal gene so offspring die as larvae; sustained releases of millions of males in Mandacaru and Juazeiro districts reduced wild larval numbers by 81 to 95 percent. CTNBio approved commercial release in April 2014 and Oxitec built a production plant in Piracicaba, while regulators withheld registration for years and critics questioned long-term suppression and gene persistence. Brazil became the main testing ground for genetically engineered insect control against dengue, Zika and chikungunya vectors.

bushehr-nuclear-grid-2011.summary: Bushehr Unit 1 connects to Iran's grid on 3 September 2011, first power reactor in region. christchurch-earthquake-2011.summary: At 12:51 pm on 22 February 2011 a shallow magnitude 6.2 aftershock of September 2010 Darfield earthquake struck beneath Christchurch's southeastern suburbs. Instruments near its source recorded vertical accelerations above 2 g, among highest ever measured in a city. Canterbury Television and Pyne Gould buildings collapsed, killing 133 of 185 dead; unreinforced masonry fell on streets. Liquefaction ejected sand and water across eastern suburbs, wrecking foundations and pipes; government later red-zoned about 8,000 residential properties as unrebuildable. Light timber-framed houses performed well structurally but suffered from ground failure. Royal Commission's 2012 report drove changes to building assessment, unreinforced masonry rules and engineering oversight.

Virologist Ali Mohamed Zaki cultures sputum on Vero cells, finds a cytopathic effect no routine test explains and sends samples to Ron Fouchier's laboratory at Erasmus MC in Rotterdam, which sequences a betacoronavirus related to bat viruses, and Zaki posts a notice on ProMED-mail on 20 September 2012. Saudi authorities object to export of samples and Zaki leaves his post. Named Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus in 2013, it passes from dromedary camels to humans and spreads in hospitals; by 2024 WHO counts about 2,600 cases and 940 deaths, mostly in Saudi Arabia, with a 2015 outbreak of 186 cases in South Korea. colombia-onchocerciasis-elimination-2013.summary: On 29 July 2013 World Health Organization verified that Colombia had eliminated transmission of Onchocerca volvulus, parasite carried by Simulium blackflies that causes river blindness. Its single focus, 1,366 people in and around Naicioná on Río Micay in Cauca department, had received ivermectin donated by Merck twice a year from 1996 with coverage above 85 percent; transmission stopped by 2007, treatments ended in 2008 and three years of surveillance found no infected flies or children. Under Onchocerciasis Elimination Program for the Americas, Ecuador followed in 2014, Mexico in 2015 and Guatemala in 2016, leaving only a Yanomami focus on Venezuela-Brazil border. disi-water-conveyance-jordan-2013.summary: King Abdullah II inaugurates Disi Water Conveyance Project on 17 July 2013. In 2009 Duke University geochemists had reported radium in Disi groundwater at levels many times above international drinking guidance, forcing Jordan to blend and monitor supply. india-polio-free-2014.summary: WHO's South-East Asia Region was certified polio free on 27 March 2014, three years after India's last wild poliovirus case, a girl in Howrah, West Bengal, on 13 January 2011. National Immunization Days delivered oral polio vaccine to about 170 million children under five in each round through 2.3 million vaccinators, with booth days, house to house sweeps, transit teams at stations and tracking of migrant families in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar. Monovalent and bivalent oral vaccines introduced from 2005 and 2010 raised efficacy against type 1 and 3. Surveillance of acute flaccid paralysis and environmental sewage sampling sustained certification.

kiribati-fiji-land-purchase-2014.summary: Kiribati's 33 atolls mostly lie under three metres above sea level. President Anote Tong's government paid about 9.3 million Australian dollars to Church of England for 2,200 hectares at Natoavatu on Fiji's Vanua Levu, completing payment in May 2014. Tong framed purchase as food security and a possible refuge under his 'migration with dignity' policy, while Fiji's prime minister Frank Bainimarama said I-Kiribati would be welcome. Among I-Kiribati, land in Fiji raised and complicated imaginings of migration. Land is hilly, partly forested and already home to descendants of Solomon Islanders; later government used it for farming rather than settlement.

nigeria-ebola-containment-2014.summary: On 20 July 2014 Patrick Sawyer, a Liberian-American already ill with Ebola, flew into Lagos, a city of over 20 million, and collapsed at the airport. Nigeria's health ministry and Lagos State turned an emergency operations centre built for polio eradication, with its GIS tools and trained field officers, into an Ebola incident command within days. Teams identified 894 contacts in Lagos and Port Harcourt and made about 18,500 home visits. Transmission ended at 19 confirmed and one probable case with eight deaths, and WHO declared Nigeria Ebola-free on 20 October 2014. Rapid isolation and contact tracing stopped an outbreak in a megacity while Guinea, Sierra Leone and Liberia were overwhelmed.

seq2seq-2014.summary: In 2014 two papers showed one network could read a sentence into a vector and another write it out in a new language. Sutskever, Vinyals and Le wrote “Sequence to sequence learning with neural networks,” and Kyunghyun Cho's Montreal group wrote “Learning Phrase Representations using RNN Encoder-Decoder for Statistical Machine Translation,” dated June 3, 2014. In seq2seq, one neural network, its encoder, compresses input such as a sentence into one vector of numbers, and a second, its decoder, expands that vector into output. Because that vector has fixed size, long inputs lost information, which attention mechanisms later addressed.

swachh-bharat-mission-2014.summary: On 2 October 2014, Gandhi's birthday, Prime Minister Narendra Modi launched the Swachh Bharat Mission with the goal of ending open defecation in rural India by 2019. Household toilet coverage stood at about 39 percent. With cash incentives of 12,000 rupees per latrine, village-level behaviour campaigns and a monitoring app, the programme recorded more than 100 million household toilets by October 2019 and declared all 600,000 villages open-defecation free; by November 2025 the count stood near 120 million. Independent surveys found usage lagging construction in some states. A 2024 study in Scientific Reports across 640 districts linked toilet construction above 30 percent of households to 5.3 fewer infant deaths per 1,000 births, roughly 60,000 to 70,000 infant deaths averted a year. Phase II, to 2026, funds solid and liquid waste management.

India hosts its secretariat at Gurugram and contributes land and seed funding; a framework agreement signed in 2016 makes it a treaty body in December 2017, later opened to all UN members, with over 100 signatories by 2024. Jha's 2023 study places it in India's climate diplomacy. Its programmes run from solar pumps to a proposed global grid interconnection.

mariana-fundao-dam-collapse-2015.summary: On 5 November 2015 Fundão iron-ore tailings dam of Samarco, a joint venture of Vale and BHP Billiton, liquefied and collapsed near Mariana, Minas Gerais. About 40 million cubic metres of slurry buried Bento Rodrigues village, killed 19 people, and travelled 650 kilometres down Rio Doce to its Atlantic mouth in 17 days, cutting water supply to 250,000 people and smothering fish and riverbank forest. Ecologists called it Brazil's worst environmental disaster, and Vale's Brumadinho dam failed in like manner in January 2019, killing 270. Investigations blamed upstream-raised construction and drainage failures under rising deposition. A 2024 settlement proposal reached about 25 billion dollars, with cases also heard in English courts.

nepal-earthquake-crisis-mapping-2015.summary: A magnitude 7.8 earthquake strikes Nepal on 25 April 2015, killing about 9,000. Kathmandu Living Labs, a small non-profit that had mapped Kathmandu Valley's buildings and roads in OpenStreetMap since 2013, cannot regroup for 20 hours, then opens a situation room in its Baluwatar office on 26 April. Working with Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team, it directs remote volunteers tracing satellite imagery: nearly 1,500 mappers within two days, several thousand within weeks, adding hundreds of thousands of buildings and roads across affected districts. It launches a crowd-reporting site, later QuakeMap.org, where villagers post needs that volunteers verify and pass to Nepal Army and Red Cross.

openai-founded-2015.summary: In December 2015 OpenAI was founded as a nonprofit with $1 billion pledged to make AI benefit everyone. Its other founders were Ilya Sutskever, Greg Brockman, Trevor Blackwell, Vicki Cheung, Andrej Karpathy, Durk Kingma, John Schulman, Pamela Vagata and Wojciech Zaremba. resnet-2015.summary: In 2015 Microsoft's ResNet showed how to train networks hundreds of layers deep, a trick now inside nearly every AI model. It won that year's ImageNet Large Scale Visual Recognition Challenge. Stacking too many layers had made networks train worse, a “degradation” problem; ResNet's layers instead learn residual functions, with skip connections that pass each layer's input forward alongside its output. That residual connection let networks hundreds of layers deep train stably, and it became a common motif in transformers such as BERT and GPT, AlphaGo Zero and AlphaFold.

Spoken translation covers English, French, German, Mandarin, Italian, Spanish, Portuguese, Arabic, Japanese and Russian.

Their stated aim is “peace and prosperity for people and the planet,” from ending poverty and hunger to tackling climate change and preserving oceans and forests, with most targets due by 2030. Theranos, a blood-testing startup valued by press at $9 billion (a Justice Department filing put its stock at over $4 billion at end 2014), claimed to run tests on a few drops of blood. Theranos called his allegations factually and scientifically erroneous, and Walgreens suspended plans to expand its blood-testing centers. Former employee Tyler Shultz was a key source. volkswagen-dieselgate-2015.summary: In September 2015 US regulators revealed Volkswagen had rigged 11 million diesel cars to cheat emissions tests. It alleged that Volkswagen and Audi cars with 2-litre TDI diesel engines sold in the US from 2009 to 2015 carried defeat-device software that switched emissions controls on only during testing, letting them emit up to 40 times legal nitrogen oxide limits in normal driving. EPA ordered 482,000 cars recalled, CEO Martin Winterkorn resigned, and by mid-2020 this scandal had cost VW $33.3 billion in fines, settlements and buybacks.

zika-brazil-microcephaly-2015.summary: Zika virus, carried by Aedes aegypti, spread through Northeast Brazil from early 2015. In October paediatric neurologists in Recife, among them Vanessa van der Linden, reported a cluster of newborns with microcephaly, and on 11 November 2015 Brazil's Ministry of Health declared a national public health emergency. On 17 November Brazilian laboratories detected Zika RNA in amniotic fluid of two affected pregnancies in Paraíba, and PAHO issued an alert. A Rio de Janeiro cohort led by Patrícia Brasil, published in New England Journal of Medicine, found abnormal outcomes in about 42 percent of infected pregnancies. WHO declared a global emergency in February 2016. Brazil recorded more than 2,000 confirmed congenital cases by 2017, concentrated among poor families in Northeast states.

addis-djibouti-railway-2016.summary: On 5 October 2016 Ethiopia's prime minister Hailemariam Desalegn and Djibouti's president Ismail Omar Guelleh opened a 752 km railway from Addis Ababa's Furi-Lebu station toward Djibouti's port, electrified at 25 kV and built from 2011 by China Railway Group and China Civil Engineering Construction Corporation for about US$4 billion, mostly on Export-Import Bank of China loans. It replaces a metre-gauge line finished in 1917 under Menelik II's concession. Djibouti's section opened in January 2017 and commercial freight and passenger service began on 1 January 2018, with a Chinese consortium operating it for six years. Power shortages, debt renegotiation and livestock strikes marked early years.

aerofarms-newark-vertical-farm-2016.summary: In September 2016 AeroFarms begins production at 212 Rome Street, Newark, New Jersey, on the site of former steel supplier Grammer, Dempsey and Hudson, filling nearly 70,000 square feet with grow tables stacked 12 layers to 36 feet, roots misted in aeroponic cloth beds under LEDs. Associated Press reports an industry group calling it the world's largest commercial vertical farm, planned at 2 million pounds of greens a year with crops in about 16 days against 30 in the field. Benke and Tomkins's 2017 review sets such farms in the context of urbanization, land scarcity and electricity cost, their binding constraint. The sector raised billions from 2017 to 2022, then AeroFarms filed for bankruptcy in June 2023 as Fifth Season closed and AppHarvest liquidated; Palm Ventures bought AeroFarms in April 2026.

amazon-prime-air-first-delivery-2016.summary: In December 2016 an Amazon drone flew a Fire TV and popcorn to a customer near Cambridge, 13 minutes from order to doorstep. Its flight, including landing, was fully autonomous and took 13 minutes from order to doorstep; drones could carry up to five pounds, in daylight only. Two customers began this trial, and Amazon planned to widen it to dozens, then hundreds, living within a few miles of its Cambridge fulfillment center.
